citations.narrative:
A regularly scheduled visit to the facility by the attending veterinarian has not occurred over the past 12 months according
to the licensee. Regularly scheduled premise visits are essential in determining if all aspects of animal care (nutrition,
health, environment, water, and air quality, etc.) are being provided to the dogs. The licensee must have regularly
scheduled visits, not less than once every 12 months, by the attending veterinarian to the facility where animals are kept,
to assess and ensure the adequacy of veterinary care and other aspects of animal care and use.
Correct by 10/02/2026.

The licensee has not been following the attending veterinarian’s approved schedule for the sampling for parasites and
other pests for dogs. According to the facility’s Program of Veterinary Care (PVC) for Dogs at least 2 dogs will be tested
for heartworm yearly and all adult dogs will have a fecal test yearly. There was no record or documentation available to
show these parasite tests had been performed. Failure to conduct sampling and treatment for parasites and other pests in
accordance with the attending veterinarians approved schedule can expose the animals to increased disease risk and can
delay treatment. The licensee must ensure that sampling and treatment of parasites and other pests (including fleas,
worms, coccidia, giardia, and heartworm) are followed in accordance with the schedule approved by the attending
veterinarian.
Correct by 10/02/2026.
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with the licensee.
